lessons.unit: Unit 1: About me
lessons.title: I, you, he, she: personal pronouns
objectives: Use أَنَا، أَنْتَ، أَنْتِ، هُوَ، هِيَ correctly
Make nominal sentences such as أَنَا طَالِبٌ
Choose masculine or feminine forms
starter: Say 'the book is on the table' in Arabic.
What do we call the little mark that doubles a sound?
Say 'my pen' and 'your pen' (to a boy) in Arabic.

teach.heading: Bismillah and pronouns
teach.note: Begin with bismillah and a short greeting dialogue (as-salaamu alaykum, kayfa haaluka). Explain that pronouns replace names so we do not repeat them. Elicit English pronouns first.

teach.heading: Four of the five
teach.note: Model each with gestures: point to self (ana), point to a boy picture (huwa), point to a girl picture (hiya). Choral drill. Common error: mixing huwa and hiya; use colour-coding.

teach.heading: You: boy and girl
teach.note: Arabic has two words for 'you'. The final vowel is the clue: fatha for a boy, kasra for a girl. Drill with two name cards, one with a boy's name and one with a girl's name. Ask pupils to choose the right word for classmates.

teach.heading: Nominal sentences
teach.note: Arabic does not need 'am/is/are' in these sentences. Say ana taalib = 'I (am) a student'. Point out the female ending ة in taaliba/mu'allima. Pupils form sentences with a pronoun and a profession.

teach.heading: Practice with jobs
teach.note: Introduce طَبِيبٌ (doctor) and مُهَنْدِسٌ (engineer) as extension vocabulary. Show pictures. Pupils say a sentence about each picture using the right pronoun. Correct mismatches between pronoun and ending.

practice: Choose the correct pronoun for each picture of a boy and girl.
Say 'she is a teacher' and 'you (girl) are a student' in Arabic.
independent: Write six sentences using different pronouns and professions.
Match pictures of people to sentences.
Role-play a short dialogue with a partner.
exit: Say 'I am a student' in Arabic.
lessons.homework: Write five sentences about your family using هِيَ، هُوَ and أَنَا.
lessons.send: SEND: pronoun cards with picture clues, sentence frames. EAL: compare with home-language pronouns. Stretch: add the adjectives كَبِيرٌ/صَغِيرٌ to describe a person.

lessons.title: Bridge: back to school; where are you from?
lessons.bigQuestion: How do I greet someone and say where I am from in Arabic?
objectives: To understand how to greet people, introduce myself and say where I am from
successCriteria: All: greet with صَبَاحُ الخَيْرِ and reply صَبَاحُ النُّورِ
Most: ask مِنْ أَيْنَ أَنْتَ؟ and answer أَنَا مِنْ ...
Some: say where someone else is from with هُوَ or هِيَ
lessons.crossCurricular: Geography: finding the countries our families come from on a world map
lessons.smsc: Cultural: the Muslim ummah comes from many countries but greets with one salam

keywords.def: where are you from? (to a boy)

hook.text: Our class may have families from many countries. How many countries do you think are in our class? How could we ask in Arabic?
hook.a: We can ask مِنْ أَيْنَ أَنْتَ؟ (min ayna anta?) and answer أَنَا مِنْ ...

islamicLink.text: Allah says He made us into nations and tribes so that we may know one another, and the most noble with Allah is the most God-fearing (al-Hujurat 49:13). Asking where someone is from helps us know one another.

starter.q: Bismillah. Reply to اَلسَّلَامُ عَلَيْكُمْ. A) وَعَلَيْكُمُ السَّلَامُ B) صَبَاحُ الخَيْرِ

teach.heading: Back to school greetings
teach.note: Begin with bismillah. Pupils greet the next pupil by name. To a girl: كَيْفَ حَالُكِ؟ (kayfa haluki?).

teach.heading: I, you, he, she
teach.note: Point to yourself, a boy, a girl on screen. Pupils say the pronoun.

teach.heading: Where are you from?
bullets: مِنْ أَيْنَ أَنْتَ؟ (min ayna anta?) to a boy
مِنْ أَيْنَ أَنْتِ؟ (min ayna anti?) to a girl
teach.note: Other countries: مِصْرَ (Misr) Egypt, تُرْكِيَا (Turkiya), بَاكِسْتَان (Bakistan). Pupils give their own.

teach.heading: He is from, she is from
bullets: No word for 'is' in Arabic here
teach.note: Arabic needs no 'is' in these sentences: huwa min Misr = he (is) from Egypt.

teach.heading: Check
teach.note: 30 seconds, then share.

check.q: How do you ask a girl where she is from?
check.why: أَنْتِ (anti) with a kasrah is 'you' to a girl.

practice.q: Answer: مِنْ أَيْنَ أَنْتَ؟ (say you are from Britain)
practice.model:
Start with أَنَا (I).
Add مِنْ (from).
Add the country: بِرِيطَانِيَا.

independent.q: Core: Write a short introduction: greeting, name, where you are from.
independent.a: For example: اَلسَّلَامُ عَلَيْكُمْ. اِسْمِي مَرْيَمُ. أَنَا مِنْ بِرِيطَانِيَا.
independent.model: Teacher writes their own three lines on the whiteboard, reading each aloud.

independent.q: Extend: Write two lines about a classmate with هُوَ or هِيَ, e.g. اِسْمُهُ آدَمُ. هُوَ مِنْ ...
independent.a: For example: اِسْمُهَا سَارَةُ. هِيَ مِنْ تُرْكِيَا.

independent.q: Stretch: Write a short dialogue of four lines between two pupils meeting for the first time.
independent.a: For example: صَبَاحُ الخَيْرِ. صَبَاحُ النُّورِ. مِنْ أَيْنَ أَنْتَ؟ أَنَا مِنْ مِصْرَ.

exit.q: What does مِنْ أَيْنَ mean? A) where from? B) how are you? C) what is your name?
Big question: greet me and tell me where you are from.
exit.a: For example: صَبَاحُ الخَيْرِ. أَنَا مِنْ بِرِيطَانِيَا.

lessons.homework: Ask two family members مِنْ أَيْنَ أَنْتَ؟ / أَنْتِ؟ and write their answers in Arabic.
lessons.send: SEND: sentence frames: أَنَا مِنْ ___. EAL: flags with country names. Stretch: use اِسْمُهُ (his name) and اِسْمُهَا (her name).

lessons.title: Bridge: how much is it? Buying food; my body
lessons.bigQuestion: How do I ask for something and its price in Arabic?
objectives: To understand how to ask how much something costs and name parts of my body
successCriteria: All: ask بِكَمْ هٰذَا؟ (bikam hadha?)
Most: say what I want: أُرِيدُ خُبْزًا (uridu khubzan)
Some: answer with a price, e.g. بِخَمْسَةِ جُنَيْهَاتٍ
lessons.smsc: Moral: honesty in buying and selling

hook.text: You are in a shop in an Arabic-speaking country. You want bread and need to know the price. What two things must you be able to say?
hook.a: What I want (أُرِيدُ) and how much is it (بِكَمْ هٰذَا؟).

islamicLink.text: Allah says: 'Give full measure and weight in justice' (al-An'am 6:152). Muslims buy and sell honestly, with fair prices and fair weights.

starter.q: Bismillah. How do you ask a boy where he is from? A) مِنْ أَيْنَ أَنْتَ؟ B) كَيْفَ حَالُكَ؟

teach.heading: In the shop
teach.note: Begin with bismillah. After أُرِيدُ the noun ends in -an: خُبْزًا, حَلِيبًا.

teach.heading: How much is it?
teach.note: جُنَيْه is a pound; for 3 to 10 we use the plural جُنَيْهَات. Pupils ask and answer with prices from ٣ to ١٠.

teach.heading: How many?
bullets: كَمْ تُفَّاحَةً؟ (kam tuffahatan?) how many apples?
teach.note: After كَمْ the noun is singular. This is a stretch point: most pupils just need كَمْ?

teach.heading: My body
teach.note: Pupils point to each part on themselves as they say it. Add my: رَأْسِي (ra'si), يَدِي (yadi).

teach.heading: Check
teach.note: 30 seconds, then share.

check.q: How do you ask the price?
check.why: بِكَمْ هٰذَا؟ means 'how much is this?'.

practice.q: Say: I want milk. How much is this?
practice.model:
Start with أُرِيدُ (I want).
Add the food with -an: حَلِيبًا.
Then ask: بِكَمْ هٰذَا؟

independent.q: Core: Write a shop dialogue of four lines: greeting, I want ..., how much?, the price.
independent.a: For example: صَبَاحُ الخَيْرِ. أُرِيدُ خُبْزًا. بِكَمْ هٰذَا؟ هٰذَا بِخَمْسَةِ جُنَيْهَاتٍ.
independent.model: Teacher writes the dialogue line by line, reading both parts.

independent.q: Extend: Write five body words with their English meaning, then read them to the class, pointing to each part as you say it.
independent.a: رَأْس، عَيْن، فَم، يَد، رِجْل

independent.q: Stretch: Ask how many: كَمْ ...؟ for apples and answer with a number.
independent.a: كَمْ تُفَّاحَةً؟ أُرِيدُ أَرْبَعَ تُفَّاحَاتٍ.

exit.q: What does أُرِيدُ mean? A) I want B) I have C) I go
Big question: ask for bread and its price in Arabic.

lessons.homework: Play shop at home: ask for three foods in Arabic and say their prices.
lessons.send: SEND: shop cards with pictures and prices. EAL: phrase card with English. Stretch: use the plural of يَد: يَدَانِ (yadani), two hands.

lessons.unit: Unit 2: Numbers and what I like
lessons.title: Food I like and do not like
objectives: Name ten foods and drinks in Arabic
Say what you like and do not like
Use Islamic manners when eating
starter: Count from six to ten in Arabic.

teach.heading: Food and drink
teach.note: Show pictures and say each word. Pupils echo. Use real examples from lunch or iftar. Ask: what do you usually drink in the morning?

teach.heading: More foods
teach.note: Dates are linked to the Sunnah of breaking the fast with dates. Pupils may know this; keep a gentle tone. Practise: say the word, then point to a picture.

teach.heading: I like
bullets: I like dates, I like juice
teach.note: Teach uhibbu + al- + noun. Note that the noun ending changes to -a after uhibbu (fatha). Model several. Pupils say what they like.

teach.heading: I do not like
teach.note: Teach laa to negate. Pupils choose something they do not like. Be sensitive: no need to criticise food. Encourage respectful language when someone dislikes something, and gratitude for food.

teach.heading: Eating with adab
teach.note: The Prophet ﷺ taught the boy 'Say Bismillah, eat with your right hand and eat from what is near you' (Sahih al-Bukhari and Muslim). Discuss manners with food. Pupils practise saying Bismillah and Alhamdulillah before and after eating.

practice: Say 'I am nine years old' in Arabic.
Count from one to ten in Arabic.
Say whether you like each food shown on the screen.
Ask a partner هَلْ تُحِبُّ ...؟ and answer with نَعَمْ or لَا.
independent: Write six sentences: three with أُحِبُّ, three with لَا أُحِبُّ.
Make a menu with five foods in Arabic.
Interview a partner and report one thing they like.
exit: How do you say 'I like dates' in Arabic?
What do we say before eating?
lessons.homework: Write a short paragraph about three foods you like and one you do not like.
lessons.send: SEND: picture menu with Arabic labels, sentence frames. EAL: share foods from home language and culture. Stretch: add 'because it is tasty' with لِأَنَّهُ لَذِيذٌ.

lessons.unit: Spring 1: My new home; my room and furniture; describing my appearance and clothes
lessons.title: My new home: the rooms
lessons.bigQuestion: How can I describe my home in Arabic?
objectives: To understand how to name the rooms of a home and describe it in simple sentences
successCriteria: All: name five rooms
Most: say فِي بَيْتِي ... (in my house there is ...)
Some: count rooms: فِي بَيْتِي ثَلَاثُ غُرَفٍ
lessons.crossCurricular: Design and technology: floor plans and how rooms are used
lessons.smsc: Spiritual: thanking Allah for a home that gives rest and safety

hook.text: If you moved to a new home, which room would you want to see first, and why?
hook.a: Any answer with a reason; today we name every room in Arabic.

islamicLink.text: Allah says He has made our homes a place of rest for us (an-Nahl 16:80). A home is a blessing to thank Allah for.

starter.q: Bismillah. What is بِكَمْ هٰذَا؟ A) How much is this? B) Where are you from?

teach.heading: Rooms in a home
teach.note: Begin with bismillah. Room = غُرْفَة; bedroom is 'room of sleep', living room is 'room of sitting'.

teach.heading: In my house there is
bullets: In my house there is a kitchen
teach.note: No word for 'there is' is needed: fi bayti + the room.

teach.heading: My new home
bullets: بَيْتِي جَدِيدٌ (bayti jadidun) my house is new
teach.note: Revise adjectives from Year 3 and 4. Pupils describe their home with one adjective.

teach.heading: How many rooms?
bullets: In my house there are three rooms
teach.note: Stretch point: with a girl word like غُرْفَة, the number has no ة: ثَلَاثُ, أَرْبَعُ.

teach.heading: Check
teach.note: 30 seconds, then share.

check.why: مَطْبَخ comes from طَبَخَ, to cook: the kitchen.

practice.q: Say: In my house there is a garden.
practice.model:
Start with فِي بَيْتِي (in my house).
Add the room: حَدِيقَةٌ.
Read it: fi bayti hadiqatun.

independent.q: Core: Draw a simple floor plan of a home (boxes) and label each room in Arabic.
independent.a: Plan labelled with مَطْبَخ، حَمَّام، غُرْفَةُ النَّوْمِ، غُرْفَةُ الجُلُوسِ، حَدِيقَة
independent.model: Teacher draws three boxes on the whiteboard and labels them مَطْبَخ، حَمَّام، غُرْفَةُ النَّوْمِ.

independent.q: Extend: Write three sentences: فِي بَيْتِي ...
independent.a: For example: فِي بَيْتِي مَطْبَخٌ. فِي بَيْتِي حَمَّامٌ. فِي بَيْتِي حَدِيقَةٌ.

independent.q: Stretch: Write how many rooms your home has, e.g. فِي بَيْتِي أَرْبَعُ غُرَفٍ.
independent.a: For example: فِي بَيْتِي أَرْبَعُ غُرَفٍ.

exit.q: What is حَدِيقَة? A) garden B) kitchen C) room
Big question: describe your home in one Arabic sentence.
exit.a: For example: بَيْتِي كَبِيرٌ وَفِيهِ حَدِيقَةٌ.

lessons.homework: Walk round your home and say the Arabic name of each room; write labels for three doors.
lessons.send: SEND: picture cards of rooms (furniture only, no people). EAL: floor plan with English and Arabic. Stretch: add وَ (and) to join two rooms in one sentence.

lessons.unit: Spring 1: My new home; my room and furniture; describing my appearance and clothes
lessons.title: My room and its furniture
lessons.bigQuestion: What is in my room, and how can I describe it in Arabic?
objectives: To understand how to name furniture and describe my room with adjectives
successCriteria: All: name five pieces of furniture
Most: say فِي غُرْفَتِي سَرِيرٌ (in my room there is a bed)
Some: add an adjective that agrees: طَاوِلَةٌ صَغِيرَةٌ
lessons.smsc: Moral: keeping my room tidy and sharing it kindly

hook.text: The word for 'chair' in Arabic is in a famous ayah many Muslims read every night. Can you guess which one?
hook.a: Ayat al-Kursi: كُرْسِيّ (kursiyy).

islamicLink.text: In Ayat al-Kursi (al-Baqarah 2:255) Allah tells us His Kursi extends over the heavens and the earth. The same word, كُرْسِيّ, is used for a chair, but nothing is like Allah.

starter.q: Bismillah. What is مَطْبَخ? A) kitchen B) bathroom
Say 'in my house there is a garden'.

teach.heading: In my room
teach.note: Begin with bismillah. Pupils turn their camera to show one item and say its name.

teach.heading: There is
bullets: In my room there is a bed
teach.note: Revise 'my' with girl words from Year 3.

teach.heading: Adjectives agree
teach.note: The adjective comes after the noun and takes ة for a girl word.

teach.heading: Check
teach.note: 30 seconds, then share.

check.q: Which is correct for 'a small table'?
check.why: طَاوِلَة is a girl word, so the adjective also takes ة, and it comes after the noun.

practice.q: Say: In my room there is a big wardrobe.
practice.model:
Start: فِي غُرْفَتِي.
The thing: خِزَانَةٌ (a girl word).
Adjective with ة: كَبِيرَةٌ.

practice.q: Boy word or girl word: نَافِذَة?

independent.q: Core: Write four sentences about your room: فِي غُرْفَتِي ...
independent.a: For example: فِي غُرْفَتِي سَرِيرٌ. فِي غُرْفَتِي كُرْسِيٌّ. فِي غُرْفَتِي نَافِذَةٌ. فِي غُرْفَتِي مَكْتَبٌ.
independent.model: Teacher writes two sentences about a room, then reads them aloud.

independent.q: Extend: Add an adjective to two of your sentences, with ة for girl words.
independent.a: For example: فِي غُرْفَتِي سَرِيرٌ كَبِيرٌ وَطَاوِلَةٌ صَغِيرَةٌ.

independent.q: Stretch: Write the plural: chair, كُرْسِيّ → كَرَاسِيّ, and use it: فِي غُرْفَتِي كَرَاسِيُّ.
independent.a: فِي غُرْفَتِي كَرَاسِيُّ (there are chairs in my room)

exit.q: What is سَرِير? A) bed B) chair C) window
Big question: describe your room in one Arabic sentence with an adjective.
exit.a: For example: فِي غُرْفَتِي سَرِيرٌ كَبِيرٌ.

lessons.homework: Stick Arabic labels on five things in your room (with permission) and read them each day.
lessons.send: SEND: furniture picture cards. EAL: label sheet with English. Stretch: use two adjectives: غُرْفَتِي كَبِيرَةٌ وَجَمِيلَةٌ.

lessons.unit: Spring 1: My new home; my room and furniture; describing my appearance and clothes
lessons.title: Where is it? In, on, under; oral check
lessons.bigQuestion: How can I say exactly where something is in Arabic?
objectives: To understand how to say where things are using فِي، عَلَى and تَحْتَ
successCriteria: All: say فِي (in), عَلَى (on), تَحْتَ (under)
Most: answer أَيْنَ ...؟ with a full sentence
Some: describe my room aloud in three sentences for the oral check
lessons.smsc: Social: helping someone find a lost thing by describing where it is

hook.text: You lost your pencil case. Your mum says 'It is on the table'. Which tiny word tells you exactly where to look?
hook.a: On. In Arabic: عَلَى ('ala).

islamicLink.text: Allah knows where everything is: not a leaf falls but He knows it (al-An'am 6:59). We use these small words to describe where things are.

starter.q: Bismillah. What is طَاوِلَة? A) table B) chair
Say 'in my room there is a bed'.

teach.heading: Where words
teach.note: Begin with bismillah. Pupils move a pen in, on, under and next to a cup on camera and say the word.

teach.heading: Where is the book?
bullets: The book is on the table
teach.note: After فِي، عَلَى، تَحْتَ the next word ends in -i (kasrah): الطَّاوِلَةِ.

teach.heading: More examples
bullets: الحَقِيبَةُ تَحْتَ السَّرِيرِ: the bag is under the bed
الثِّيَابُ فِي الخِزَانَةِ: the clothes are in the wardrobe
الكُرْسِيُّ بِجَانِبِ المَكْتَبِ: the chair is next to the desk
teach.note: Pupils read each and act it with real objects.

teach.heading: Check
teach.note: 30 seconds, then share.

options: The bag is on the bed
The bag is under the bed
The bag is in the bed

teach.heading: Oral check: describe a room
teach.note: Each pupil speaks for 30 seconds while others work. Record: names rooms and furniture; uses a position word; adjective agrees.

practice.q: Answer: أَيْنَ الكِتَابُ؟ (it is in the bag)
practice.model:
Start with the thing: الكِتَابُ.
Add where: فِي (in).
Add the place with -i: الحَقِيبَةِ.

practice.q: Say 'the chair is next to the window'.

independent.q: Core: Look at a picture of a room (portal worksheet) and write four 'where' sentences.
independent.a: For example: السَّرِيرُ بِجَانِبِ النَّافِذَةِ. الكِتَابُ عَلَى الطَّاوِلَةِ. الحَقِيبَةُ تَحْتَ الكُرْسِيِّ. الثِّيَابُ فِي الخِزَانَةِ.

lessons.crossCurricular: Computing: healthy screen time and online safety

hook.text: Is time spent on games wasted, or can it be good? What makes the difference?
hook.a: It depends how much and what: time is a blessing, so we use it wisely and keep salah and family first.

islamicLink.text: The Prophet ﷺ said: 'There are two blessings in which many people are cheated: health and free time' (Bukhari).

starter.a: For example: أَقْرَأُ القُرْآنَ بَعْدَ الفَجْرِ

teach.heading: Devices
teach.note: Begin with Bismillah. Hold up or point to each. Spoken practice only; no songs or music.

teach.heading: What I do
bullets: أَتَعَلَّمُ عَلَى الجِهَازِ: I learn on the device
teach.note: Pupils say one true sentence.

teach.heading: Wise or not?
teach.note: Pupils show the column number.

teach.heading: Quick check
teach.note: 30 seconds, then share.

practice.q: Say: I play a game on the computer for one hour.
practice.a: أَلْعَبُ لُعْبَةً عَلَى الحَاسُوبِ سَاعَةً وَاحِدَةً
practice.model: Teacher builds it: أَلْعَبُ (I play) + لُعْبَةً (a game) + عَلَى الحَاسُوبِ (on the computer) + سَاعَةً وَاحِدَةً (for one hour).

independent.q: Screen-time plan on the pupil PDF: three Arabic sentences about devices you use, when and for how long; then one rule in English for using them wisely. Start: أَلْعَبُ ...
independent.a: Three correct sentences with a device, a time word and a duration; one wise rule
independent.model: Teacher writes: أَسْتَعْمِلُ الحَاسُوبَ بَعْدَ المَدْرَسَةِ سَاعَةً وَاحِدَةً.

independent.q: Extend: add a reason with لِأَنَّ.
independent.a: For example: أَلْعَبُ قَلِيلًا لِأَنَّ الوَقْتَ مُهِمٌّ

independent.q: Stretch: say 'I do not play during salah time': لَا أَلْعَبُ وَقْتَ الصَّلَاةِ.
independent.a: لَا أَلْعَبُ وَقْتَ الصَّلَاةِ

exit.q: حَاسُوب is ...
Back to our ponder: wasted or good?
exit.a: It depends: used wisely and in moderation, after duties

hook.text: If someone read a paragraph about your week, what would they learn about you?
hook.a: Pupils' own: what matters to us, like salah, family, learning and play.

islamicLink.text: The Prophet ﷺ said: 'The most beloved deeds to Allah are the most regular, even if small' (Bukhari and Muslim).

teach.heading: Building blocks
teach.note: Begin with Bismillah.

teach.heading: Model paragraph
teach.note: Labelled: time, action, joiner, opinion.

quote.text:
كُلَّ يَوْمٍ أَقْرَأُ القُرْآنَ بَعْدَ الفَجْرِ.
يَوْمَ السَّبْتِ أَذْهَبُ إِلَى المَسْجِدِ، ثُمَّ أَلْعَبُ مَعَ أَخِي.
يَوْمَ الجُمُعَةِ أُصَلِّي الجُمُعَةَ.
أُحِبُّ يَوْمَ الجُمُعَةِ لِأَنَّهُ يَوْمٌ مُبَارَكٌ.

teach.heading: Checklist
bullets: A day or time word in each sentence
teach.note: Pupils check their own work against this.

practice.model: Teacher: two actions in order, so put ثُمَّ between them: أَذْهَبُ إِلَى المَدْرَسَةِ ثُمَّ أَرْجِعُ إِلَى البَيْتِ.

lessons.title: My relatives: أَقَارِبِي
lessons.bigQuestion: Why do you think Islam puts so much reward on visiting and helping relatives?
objectives: To understand and use words for relatives with 'my' and describe them in sentences
successCriteria: All: say six relatives with 'my'
Most: describe two relatives with a job or an age
Some: write a short paragraph about my relatives with وَ and لٰكِنْ

keywords.def: my cousin (son of my father's brother)

hook.text: Why do you think Islam puts so much reward on visiting and helping relatives?
hook.a: Keeping family ties brings blessing in provision and life (Bukhari and Muslim).

islamicLink.text: The Prophet ﷺ said: 'Whoever would like his provision to be increased and his life to be extended, let him keep the ties of kinship' (Bukhari and Muslim).

starter.q: Say a day of the week in Arabic.
Which month is the month of fasting?

teach.heading: My relatives
teach.note: Begin with Bismillah. Pupils repeat. Spoken practice only; no songs or music.

teach.heading: Describing a relative
bullets: عَمِّي طَبِيبٌ (my uncle is a doctor)
خَالَتِي مُعَلِّمَةٌ (my aunt is a teacher)
teach.note: Jobs agree: مُعَلِّمٌ / مُعَلِّمَةٌ.

check.q: 'My aunt (mother's sister) is a teacher' is ...
check.why: خَالَة + ي, and the feminine job.

practice.q: Say: my uncle is a doctor.
practice.model: Teacher: who? عَمِّي. What is he? طَبِيبٌ. Arabic needs no 'is': عَمِّي طَبِيبٌ.

independent.q: Write a paragraph about three relatives on the pupil PDF (names may be changed): who they are, a job or age, and where they live or when you visit.
independent.a: Five or six correct sentences, for example: عَمِّي مُهَنْدِسٌ. يَسْكُنُ قَرِيبًا مِنَّا. أَزُورُهُ يَوْمَ الجُمُعَةِ.
independent.model: Teacher writes about an example relative: جَدِّي عُمُرُهُ سَبْعُونَ سَنَةً. يَسْكُنُ فِي بَيْتٍ كَبِيرٍ.

independent.q: Extend: join two sentences with لٰكِنْ (but).
independent.a: For example: خَالِي طَبِيبٌ لٰكِنَّ عَمِّي مُعَلِّمٌ

exit.q: أَقَارِبُ means ...
Back to our ponder: why visit relatives?
exit.a: Keeping ties brings blessing (Bukhari and Muslim)

Some: add times with قَبْلَ and بَعْدَ

hook.text: What is the hardest part of fasting, and what is the best part?
hook.a: Answers vary: hunger or thirst; iftar with family, extra prayer and reward from Allah.

islamicLink.text: Allah says: 'O you who have believed, fasting has been prescribed for you as it was prescribed for those before you, that you may become righteous' (al-Baqarah 2:183).

teach.heading: My Ramadan day
teach.note: Begin with Bismillah. Pupils repeat each verb with actions. Spoken practice only; no songs or music.

teach.heading: 'I' verbs start with أَ or أُ
teach.note: Spot the first letter: أَ = I.

options: I break my fast with dates
check.why: أُفْطِرُ = I break my fast; التَّمْر = dates.

practice.model: Teacher: أَصُومُ (I fast), فِي (in), رَمَضَانَ (Ramadan). Together: أَصُومُ فِي رَمَضَانَ.

independent.q: Write 'my Ramadan day' on the pupil PDF: five sentences in order using the verbs and قَبْلَ or بَعْدَ.
independent.a: For example: أَتَسَحَّرُ قَبْلَ الفَجْرِ. أَصُومُ. أَقْرَأُ القُرْآنَ. أُفْطِرُ عَلَى التَّمْرِ. أُصَلِّي التَّرَاوِيحَ.
independent.model: Teacher writes sentence 1: أَتَسَحَّرُ قَبْلَ الفَجْرِ.

independent.q: Extend: add 'with my family': مَعَ عَائِلَتِي.
independent.a: أُفْطِرُ مَعَ عَائِلَتِي

exit.q: السَّحُورُ is ...
Back to our ponder: best part of fasting?

lessons.smsc: Spiritual and social: celebrating Eid as worship with family

hook.text: What makes Eid different from any other happy day?
hook.a: It is worship too: Eid prayer, takbir, giving and visiting family, for the sake of Allah.

islamicLink.text: Anas reported that the Prophet ﷺ would not go out on the morning of Eid al-Fitr until he had eaten some dates (Bukhari).

starter.q: Say 'I break my fast with dates'.

teach.heading: Two Eids
teach.note: Begin with Bismillah. Spoken practice only; no songs or music.

teach.heading: On Eid I ...
teach.note: Pupils repeat with actions.

head: Arabic
English
rows: I eat dates before the prayer (Eid al-Fitr)

teach.heading: Giving a reason
bullets: I like Eid because it is a day of joy

practice.q: Say: I like Eid because I visit my relatives.
practice.model: Teacher: أُحِبُّ العِيدَ, then the reason with لِأَنَّنِي (because I), then أَزُورُ أَقَارِبِي.

independent.q: Eid card text on the pupil PDF (a geometric border, no people): write four sentences about what you do on Eid and why you like it, and the greeting عِيدٌ مُبَارَكٌ.

exit.q: 'Eid Mubarak' in Arabic is ...

exit.a: It is worship and joy together
